description:
Hello! We’re from Córdoba, Argentina.

We’re developing a game for the NASA Space Apps Challenge where you design your own spacecraft, conduct experiments in laboratories, and play as part of a four-person team. You’ll make decisions during space missions across the galaxy—all while having fun, managing limited resources, facing unexpected challenges, and carrying out rescue operations.

If you enjoy adventure and exploration games, come join the adventure! We’d love to have you on board!
summary:
We developed a browser-based exploration video game built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It requires no installation: players just open the index.html file. The game puts players in high-stress mission scenarios where they must make quick decisions, and every choice has a positive or negative impact on the future of the mission.
It addresses the challenge of working under pressure by letting players practice decision-making in a safe, simulated environment. This helps people who enjoy managing situations but aren’t used to stress build the resilience to act and decide well in demanding moments.
It matters because it reflects a real-life truth: decisions have consequences. To keep the game accessible despite its text-heavy missions, we prioritized readability and are adding a tutorial system.

Direct link to the game:
https://walygchq-pixel.github.io/the-last-expedition/
details:
What does it do and how does it work?

Basically, it’s a video game built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript that runs in the browser. It’s easy to start, since all you have to do is open the index.html file. The game is about exploration and puts you in highly stressful situations where you have to make quick decisions. As a result, it helps you adapt to those kinds of circumstances. Every decision has an impact, positive or negative, on the future of the mission. I think that’s the benefit it offers.

Question 3: What is the intended impact of the project?

I think it can be a useful game for people who enjoy managing things but aren’t used to working under pressure. It can help them build the resilience needed to act in high-pressure moments and make the best decisions in situations like that.

Next question: What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software were used to develop the project?

We used a home computer with a 16-core Ryzen 1700X processor and 32 GB of RAM. We also used Visual Studio Code to review and edit the code. In addition, we used a coding agent called Gentle Shell, a project that helped us a lot to develop the game properly, avoid ambiguities in the code, and keep the number of errors or bugs to a minimum.

We used JavaScript, CSS (a style sheet language), and HTML, the markup language used throughout the project.

Next question: In what way is your project creative?

We think that whenever someone makes decisions, there are always consequences. That’s why we wanted to bring that real-life nature into the game and focus on how each person’s actions can affect how the game develops in the future.

Next question: What factors did your team take into account?

Although the development time was very short, we considered how players should interact with the game. Since it has many variables, especially in the mission design, we wanted to prioritize readability. Because it contains a lot of text, it can be cumbersome or hard to read when trying to understand the game. That’s why we’re also adding a tutorial system, so that learning to play is easier and it’s clear how everything works.
